name: RV park / resort
summary: Cost per site is driven by wastewater (municipal sewer vs. septic/drainfield vs. package plant), electrical service (50A pedestals and distribution), road and pad surfacing (gravel vs. asphalt/concrete) and how much building (bathhouse, clubhouse, store, pool) is spread over the sites. Public-sector bid-grade evidence (Missouri, Utah state parks) runs $50k-$112k per site; private-developer itemizations run roughly $15k-$40k per site. The default sits between them, weighted toward private development; confidence is medium.

typicalSize.method: OH Weekly cost model assumes a 100+ site park (e8); public examples are 35 sites (e7, Utah) and 48 sites (e21, Oregon); Richmond BC feasibility modeled 150 pads (e20). Mid 100 sites; range covers small rural parks to large resort parks.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Richmond BC feasibility modeled 150 pads on 12 acres = 12.5 sites/acre including clubhouse, pool and storage (e20). Low = resort parks with large pull-throughs and amenities; high = tight back-in parks.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Each site carries its own tow/towed vehicle space on the pad; add ~0.1 per site of visitor/office parking. Planning judgment, not sourced.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Two clusters of evidence. (a) Private-developer itemization: OH Weekly $30k-$40k per site all-in excluding land (e8, 2024), less ~$2.5k/site of surveys/engineering/permits = ~$27.5k-$37.5k hard, midpoint ~$32.5k. Freakonomics/industry estimate $15k-$25k per site for infrastructure (e11, 2025) and Menahga MN $9.2k materials per site (e12) mark the low end. (b) Public bid-grade estimates (prevailing wage, concrete pads, demolition of old loops): Missouri State Parks construction+site work per site = $78.6k (LOSP), $65.8k (St. Francois), $67.5k (Table Rock), $94.4k (Long Branch), $49.8k (Roaring River) in 2020 dollars (e1-e5), median ~$67.5k; Missouri's stated average $55k (e6); Utah Sand Hollow award $3.92M / 35 sites = ~$112k incl. restroom/shower building and day-use parking (e7, 2022). Mid = 0.75 x private ($32.5k) + 0.25 x public median ($67.5k, 2020$ used unescalated) = $41.3k, rounded to $42k, expressed as 2024 dollars (private evidence year). Low $18k = gravel roads/pads, municipal sewer available, minimal buildings (e11). High $95k = public-grade or resort build with concrete pads, paved roads, large amenity buildings (Long Branch e4; Sand Hollow e7 is an upper outlier). Evidence years span 2020-2025; Missouri 2020 figures not escalated by hand.

scope.notes: Per-site contractor price incl. general conditions and OH&P, including grading, roads, pads/patios, on-site water/sewer/electric distribution, hookups (water, sewer, 30/50A pedestal) and a share of the bathhouse/laundry/office buildings. Excludes land, soft costs, FF&E, off-site utility extensions, tap/impact fees, and on-site wastewater treatment (septic/package plant) which is a separate line item.

qualityTiers.method: Economy ~= low/mid of the hard-cost range (18k/42k = 0.43) tempered to 0.55 because the low anchor is infrastructure-only; luxury ~= high/mid (95k/42k = 2.26); premium interpolated.

systemSplit.method: Built from the OH Weekly per-site itemization (e8-e10), hard items only (total ~$33.1k): grading $2.4k -> 31 (0.073); paving $3.6k + patios/walkways $3.2k + half of landscaping/misc -> 32 (0.351 incl. site furnishings); sewer $2.5k + water $2.4k -> 33 (0.148); electrical $4.0k -> 26 (0.121); buildings $7.5k (midpoint) split across 03/06/07/08/09/10/22/23 per a typical small wood-frame bathhouse/clubhouse (0.227); remaining misc -> 01 general conditions (0.08).

lineItems.name: RV power pedestal (50/30/20A) incl. setting and connection

cost.method: Pedestal hardware $500-$600 each (e13) plus setting, breakers, metering and labor; OH Weekly total electrical incl. distribution is ~$4.0k/site (e9), of which the pedestal and its final connection taken as ~half (mid $2.0k).

lineItems.notes: Carve-out of the per-site hard cost. Distribution feeders/transformers are additional within the $4k/site electrical budget.

lineItems.name: Water and sewer hookups per site (riser, hose bib, 4in sewer inlet, laterals)

cost.method: OH Weekly sewer lines ~$2.5k + water lines ~$2.4k per site = $4.9k (e8). High reflects deep sewer, rock, or freeze-protected risers.

lineItems.name: RV pad and patio (gravel, asphalt or concrete pad; concrete patio)

cost.method: OH Weekly patios/walkways ~$3.2k per site (e8). Low = gravel pad with no patio; high = full-length concrete pad + patio (Missouri sites have concrete pads, e1).

lineItems.name: Interior park roads (20-24 ft, gravel to asphalt)

cost.method: OH Weekly paving ~$3.6k per site (e8) over an assumed ~35-45 LF of road per site (half of a double-loaded 70-90 ft site frontage + entry/loop share) = ~$90-$100/LF; low = aggregate surface, high = full-depth asphalt with curb/drainage.

lineItems.notes: Carve-out. LF per site is a planning assumption; verify against site plan.

lineItems.name: Bathhouse / comfort station with showers and laundry

cost.method: Public comparables: Oregon State Parks standard prototype restroom/shower building $1.1M (e16, 2024); South Dakota Palisades SP comfort station low bid $705,540 (e17, 2023). Mid = SD figure; high = OR prototype; low = private prefab/smaller building. Typically one per 50-75 sites.

lineItems.notes: Carve-out of the buildings share of the per-site cost (OH Weekly buildings $5k-$10k per site, e10). Add a second building above ~75 sites.

cost.method: OH Weekly buildings (clubhouse, bathhouses, amenities) $5k-$10k per site (e10); for a 100-site park that is $0.5M-$1.0M total, of which ~$0.6M assumed for office/store/clubhouse after the bathhouse. High = resort clubhouse.

lineItems.name: RV dump (sanitary) station with rinse water

cost.method: Planning judgment: concrete apron, inlet, holding/connection to sewer, rinse hydrant and approach paving. No public bid tab found in this session; verify with a local bid.

lineItems.name: On-site septic system / drainfield (no municipal sewer)

cost.method: OH Weekly: small parks have done their entire septic for ~$100k, while individual leach fields at a dozen-plus-site park cost that much (e14). Mid assumes a 100-site park with large-capacity drainfields; high = engineered/pressure-dosed systems.

lineItems.notes: Switch on when no municipal sewer is available. Scales with site count.

lineItems.name: Package wastewater treatment plant

cost.method: OH Weekly: treatment plants required by some jurisdictions 'cost $1MM plus' (e15). Mid/high are judgment for larger parks; verify with engineer.

lineItems.notes: Alternative to the septic line item; do not enable both.

lineItems.name: Sewage lift station

cost.method: Planning judgment for a duplex submersible station with controls and force main stub. Oregon Fort Stevens campground project included a south lift station within its $14.6M utility scope (e16 context) but the station was not priced separately.

lineItems.notes: Needed when gravity sewer to the outfall is not possible.

lineItems.name: Water well, pressure tank and treatment (no municipal water)

cost.method: Planning judgment: public water system well(s) sized for 100 sites incl. storage/pressure and disinfection. Verify locally (public water system rules apply).

lineItems.notes: Switch on for rural sites without municipal water.

cost.method: Planning judgment for a commercial (public-code) pool with deck, fence and equipment building. Richmond BC generic park program included a pool (e20).

perPrimaryUnit.method: Picnic table + fire ring/grill per site (~$500-$1,000) plus a per-site share of clubhouse/office/laundry furnishings and equipment for a 100-site park. Judgment; not sourced.

pctOfHard.method: Missouri State Parks 'Design and Bidding' = ~11.4% of construction + site work on four of five project sheets (e18); OH Weekly surveys/engineering/plans/permits ~$2.5k per site = ~7.6% of ~$33k hard (e8). Mid 12% adds legal, insurance and permitting; high for jurisdictions requiring CUP/rezoning and wastewater permitting.

softCosts.notes: Excludes franchise fees (e.g., KOA) and financing.

design.method: Concept-stage parks often lack a geotech/perc test; judgment.

hard.method: Missouri State Parks carried 15% contingency on concept estimates (e19); 10% mid for a designed private project.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Min ~= Freakonomics/industry low infrastructure-only figure (e11) plus minimal soft cost; max ~= Missouri LOSP total project cost $98k/site (e1) and Long Branch $118k/site (e4) in 2020 dollars, plus Utah Sand Hollow $112k/site hard (e7) with soft costs.

evidence.region: Lake of the Ozarks State Park, MO

source.title: Lake of the Ozarks State Park - Campground Upgrade Project (revenue bond project sheet)

evidence.quote: Construct 25 Campsites $1,769,000 / Other Infrastructure $196,556 / Design and Bidding $224,125 / 15% Contingency $265,350 / TOTAL PROJECT COST $2,455,031
evidence.scopeNotes: Value = (1,769,000 + 196,556) / 25 sites. Full hookup: concrete pads, 50-amp, sewer, water. Replaces 29 basic sites (demolition included). Total project cost incl. design and contingency = $98,201/site. Original mostateparks.com URL now returns 404; text read from the Internet Archive copy. Sheets state estimates are based on 2020 information.

evidence.scopeNotes: Value = (3,729,750 + 414,417) / 63. New 63-site loop with 50-amp, sewer and water at each site and 'a small showerhouse'. Original URL now 404; read from Internet Archive copy.

source.title: RV Park construction in West TD could move forward with $1 million state grant

evidence.quote: The grant requires an $884,900 local match, bringing the total estimated project cost to $1,884,900.
evidence.scopeNotes: 1,884,900 / 48 full-hookup sites. Completion of a partly built park: 'The previous owner completed most of the utility work', so this understates a ground-up build. Includes ADA restroom/shower facility.

openQuestions: Private-sector RV park bid tabs or lender feasibility budgets (SBA 7a / USDA B&I) would firm up the private-developer cluster, which currently rests on one trade newsletter.
Missouri State Parks figures are 2020 concept estimates; actual bid results (e.g., Roaring River bid tab on oa.mo.gov) should be pulled and compared.
Dump station, lift station, well and pool line items are judgment-only; need bid tabs.
KOA franchise disclosure (Item 7 initial investment) could provide a national per-site range; not retrieved in this session.
